book.nwyfre.book_of_nwyfre.name: Book of Nwyfre
book.nwyfre.book_of_nwyfre.subtitle: Of Breath and Spirit
book.nwyfre.book_of_nwyfre.landing_text: The life-breath moves through all things. Learn to hear it, and it will answer.
nwyfre.entry.about.page1: $(thing)Nwyfre$() is the life-breath that runs beneath the world - in stone and storm, in root and blood.$(br2)This book fills itself as you learn. What you have not yet earned, you will not yet read.
nwyfre.category.rituals.desc: Of chalk and bowl, of offering and hour.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_overview.page1: A rite is a bargain struck with the breath beneath the world. You draw its shape, you set out what you mean to give, and you ask.$(br2)Every rite needs three things: a $(thing)circle$() of chalk, an $(thing)altar$() at its heart, and $(thing)bowls$() set at the quarters.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_overview.page2: Place the altar. Draw the marks. Set your offerings in their bowls. Then hold the rite's $(thing)token$() and touch the altar.$(br2)If nothing answers, the circle will tell you what it lacks. Watch for the lights.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_overview.page3: The $(thing)Lesser Circle$() is the first shape you will learn: a ring of marks seven paces across, with the altar at its centre and a bowl set to each of the four quarters.$(br2)Larger shapes exist. They ask more.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_circles.page1: The marks are not decoration. They are the walls of the vessel, and a vessel with a gap holds nothing.$(br2)A mark will not cling to air. Lay it on something solid, or it falls away.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_circles.page2: Circles do not turn. North is north, and a shape drawn sideways is no shape at all.$(br2)This matters more than it sounds: the quarters carry meaning, and a rite laid the wrong way round will be asking the wrong things of the wrong powers.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_circles.page3: A single drawn mark. Many of them, in the right arrangement, make a circle.
nwyfre.entry.ogham.page1: Ogham is not drawn. It is cut, along an edge, and the edge is the letter as much as the scores are.$(br2)That edge is the $(italic)stem$(). Lay two marks beside one another and their stems meet, and the line runs on unbroken. Lay them apart and you have two sayings, not one.
nwyfre.entry.ogham.page2: Every letter is scores against the stem, and where they fall is the whole of it.$(br2)Beneath the line: $(italic)B L F S N$(), one score to five.$(br)Above it: $(italic)H D T C Q$().$(br)Slanting across: $(italic)M G NG Z R$().$(br)Square across: $(italic)A O U E I$().
nwyfre.entry.ogham.page3: Five more stand apart from the four families, each its own shape rather than a tally: the hatch, the crossing, the elbow, the lozenge, the saltire.$(br2)A mark will not cling to air. Lay it on something solid, as you would any chalk.
nwyfre.entry.ogham.page4: A length of bare stem, carrying the line and saying nothing. Use it to begin a saying, to end one, and to hold a gap between words.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_offerings.page1: Each quarter of a circle answers to an element, and each element wants its own kind of gift.$(br2)$(li)North - $(thing)Earth$()$(li)East - $(thing)Air$()$(li)South - $(thing)Fire$()$(li)West - $(thing)Water$()
nwyfre.entry.ritual_offerings.page2: Set one offering in each bowl the rite asks for. A bowl it does not ask for must be left $(thing)empty$() - a cluttered circle is an unclear question, and an unclear question gets no answer.$(br2)Offerings are taken slowly, as the rite works. Break the circle part-way and you will get back whatever it had not yet used.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_offerings.page3: Holds one offering, and only one. Right-click to give; right-click empty-handed to take back.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_augments.page1: Some rites can be bent. Leave certain things in a $(thing)chest$() near the circle and the rite will notice them, and answer differently.$(br2)An augment is not an offering. It sits apart, and it is not consumed - it is a weight on the scales, not a coin in the hand.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_augments.page2: What a rite notices is decided when it $(thing)begins$(). Emptying the chest half-way through changes nothing; the bargain is already struck.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_persistent.page1: Most rites are a single asking, answered and done. Some instead bind themselves into a $(thing)candle$().$(br2)Use a candle as the rite's token. When the working finishes, the candle is left on the altar, lit, and the rite goes on working for as long as it burns.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_persistent.page2: Touch the altar to snuff the candle, and touch it again to relight it. An unlit candle $(thing)does not burn down$() - set it aside for when you need it.$(br2)An altar holding a standing flame is busy. It will not take another rite until the candle is spent or taken away.
nwyfre.entry.ritual_diagnostics.page1: A silent circle is not a broken one. Touch the altar and it will show you what is wrong.$(br2)$(li)Lights on empty ground - marks are missing there$(li)Lights on bare stone - a bowl belongs there$(li)It names a token - you hold the wrong thing$(li)It names an element - that bowl wants filling$(li)It speaks of the hour - the circle is ready, but the moment is not
nwyfre.entry.rite_of_sunrise.page1: Hurries the night along, as sleep does.$(br2)$(li)Token: $(thing)Clock$()$(li)South: $(thing)coal$()$(li)East: $(thing)Feather$()$(br)Only at $(thing)night$() - there is nothing to hurry at noon.
nwyfre.entry.rite_of_sunrise.page2: Leave an $(thing)Eye of Ender$() in a chest nearby and the rite turns the other way, pulling the sun down instead of up.
nwyfre.entry.rite_of_clear_skies.page1: Calms the weather.$(br2)$(li)Token: $(thing)Wheat Seeds$()$(li)West: $(thing)Water Bucket$()$(li)East: $(thing)Feather$()$(br)The circle must rest on $(thing)soil$(), and this asking carries only in the overworld.
nwyfre.entry.rite_of_clear_skies.page2: Leave a $(thing)Nautilus Shell$() in a chest nearby and the rite inverts: instead of calming the sky, it calls a storm down on it.
nwyfre.entry.vigil_of_mending.page1: A standing flame that knits flesh back together for sixteen paces in every direction.$(br2)$(li)Token: $(thing)Candle$()$(li)North: $(thing)Golden Carrot$()$(li)West: $(thing)Glistering Melon Slice$()
nwyfre.entry.vigil_of_mending.page2: Leave a $(thing)Diamond$() in a chest nearby and the vigil reaches further.$(br2)The candle burns for a day of working before it is spent. Snuff it when you are away.
nwyfre.entry.rite_of_first_breath.page1: The first rite, and the smallest. It asks almost nothing, and gives back a shard of the breath made solid.$(br2)$(li)Token: $(thing)Stick$()$(li)North: $(thing)Dirt$()$(br)No hour, no weather, no place is required. If it does not answer, the circle is wrong - and the circle will tell you so.
nwyfre.entry.rite_of_first_breath.page2: Draw four marks at the corners, set a bowl due $(thing)north$() of the altar, and put a block of dirt in it. Hold a stick and touch the altar.$(br2)Leave $(thing)Glowstone Dust$() in a chest nearby and the rite gives four shards instead of one.
